graphEvents.label: What does the brief cost per prompt and what can be cut
The cost script measures the outage line at HEAD
The live brief is 296 bytes first message and 78 steady state

label: measure-brief-cost.mjs at HEAD reports median 361 bytes, min 361, max 408 because every row is the fail-open outage line plus the constant block, not a brief.

The script's fresh socket directory cannot reach a live daemon when one holds the workspace, so the arm it measures is decided by daemon state; the same four rows read 361 bytes sandboxed and 286 to 308 live with command and policy.
The live brief did not grow: 44 of 44 typed rows carry command and policy, total 13,173 bytes, median 296, range 284 to 336, against phase 011's 12,771 and 299.
The constant block is 218 bytes (12 label plus 206 hygiene) and a head is 78 bytes median, so a first prompt costs 296 bytes and 74 tokens and later prompts cost the head alone at 20 tokens.
Every head field is load-bearing: provenance 10 bytes, freshness 6, policy 8, scores 10, pass marker 6, and the only redundant token is the 12-byte Directives label paid once per session.
The started command document dominates token cost at a median 4,524 bytes (about 1,131 tokens), so the brief is 1.7 percent of it at steady state and no 22-byte cut can change a start decision.
The embedder lane is warm at 7.89 ms median and 9.85 ms p95 over 30 samples with 335.7 MB loaded; the cold sample is unavailable because the model was already loaded and this run may not unload it.

Typed prompts with a cold prompt cache cost 333.95 ms median and 547.86 ms p95 at the hook, well inside the 2,500 ms budget, while the recorded cold bounds remain 538.53 ms for the embedder and 611 to 844 ms for a true first prompt.
